Draft guidance below (will attach a clean matrix to send to ACME):

Summary: three recommended scenarios with gating and approvals. Attachment: [acme-approval-matrix.xlsx]

Scenario 1 — Quick Pilot (recommended for initial proof of value)
- Term: 6 months
- Discount: up to 30% off list (pilot pricing)
- TCV cap: $0–$50k requires Sales Manager sign-off only
- Procurement: optional but encouraged; no VP sign-off required
- Notes: Use AWS private offer if buyer insists on Marketplace billing; otherwise we can do a short SOW for services and run a separate pilot.

Scenario 2 — Standard Annual Commit
- Term: 12 months
- Discount: 18–22% off list depending on usage bands
- TCV band: $50k–$250k requires Procurement approval; Sales Director looped for discounts >20%
- Notes: Recommended default for customers expecting production usage and predictable pricing.

Scenario 3 — Enterprise Multi-year
- Term: 24–36 months with ramped pricing
- Discount: 25–40% depending on upfront commit and co-sell incentives
- TCV: >$250k requires VP/Revenue Ops sign-off and Legal redline review
- Notes: Offer expanded support, custom SLA, and optional private deployment options.

Other considerations:
- Co-sell stacking: AWS incentives may be available but need AWS PM coordination; do not promise stacked discounts until we have confirmation.
- Signing cadence: for Marketplace private offers we typically need Procurement + Authorized Signer on buyer side; internal approvals depend on discount and TCV.
- Security: if ACME needs KMS/HSM we should surface LA/SE early — Lauren, can you confirm KMS options and any onboarding latency?

I’ll attach the matrix and a short blurb we can send to Marta that maps approvals to signatures. If we want to be aggressive on the pilot, we can approve 30% for under $50k; anything above requires at least Procurement sign-off.
